findings.text: non-blocking: stop_neo4j_job runs _run_remote(f"scancel {job_id}", check=False) and discards the returned output, so the scheduler cancel prints nothing; goal requirement 6 states that the scheduler cancel and each signal print what they did, and check=False also hides a failing scancel until the later job-exit wait expires. No safety impact, because a scancel that did not take effect surfaces through _wait_for_job_exit raising, but this is the one stated goal item the node leaves unmet.

non-blocking: _signal_pids builds `if kill -<sig> <pid> 2>/dev/null; then echo SIG..; else echo "PID <pid> already gone"; fi`, which collapses every failure (EPERM, EINVAL) into the single claim that the pid was already gone, so a signal refused for lack of permission is reported as a process that had exited; goal requirement 6 asks each signal to print what it did.

non-blocking: test_lock_cleanup_refuses_while_a_process_holds_the_store asserts only that no collected script contains `pkill`; it does not assert that the lock-removal script never ran, so a reordering that executed the rm -f / dd clean script and raised afterwards would still pass this test while destroying the locks it guards.

non-blocking: the embed stop path in embed.py still decides whether to stop by `pgrep -u $USER -f "iter-codex embed start"` (and again at line 679 with `iter-codex embed`), so a server the pgrep misses is never handed to the new recorded-pid selector and survives the stop; the file is outside the node's declared write paths and the worker recorded it under outside_scope, so the repair belongs to a follow-up node rather than this one.
